title: S&P 500 Drawdowns Since 1999
subtitle: Worst falls for today's S&P 500 and for all 500 stocks of 1999
description:
Two tables built from daily adjusted closes with dividends reinvested, January 4, 1999 to October 13, 2026.

drawdowns-since-1999.csv covers the 343 current S&P 500 members that traded in 1999. 317 of them fell 50% or more at least once. The median worst fall was 71%, against 55% for the index. 303 recovered with a median trip of 5.8 years, and 40 have not made it back.

drawdowns-1999-class.csv covers all 500 stocks in the S&P 500 on January 4, 1999, including the 271 that stopped trading. 179 are still in the index, 50 left and still trade, 238 left through a buyout or merger, and 33 went bankrupt. Between 74% and 80% fell by half, and between 36% and 41% never got back to the high before their worst fall. Stocks that left use quarterly high and low prices from SEC filings, which is why those figures are ranges.

Write-up and charts at https://portfolioautopsy.pages.dev/research/drawdowns-since-1999. The tables hold derived statistics only, no raw prices.
